A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support comparison; retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original regression and Lotka–Volterra simulations, flow-cytometry graph-selection results, and supplementary sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds simulated cluster-count selection and decision-tree selection on gene-expression data.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure remains bagging model weights followed by the inflated argmax. Algorithm 1 and Definition 4.1 are unchanged. The clustering and decision-tree applications instantiate the existing framework rather than introduce a new stabilization component.

E1.justification: v3 adds two distinct tasks beyond the retained variable-selection applications: selecting the number of clusters in simulated Gaussian-mixture data (Section 5.3 and Appendix G), and selecting decision-tree structures for stem-cell classification from gene expression (Appendix H).

E2.justification: The competing selection rules remain unbagged argmax, bagged argmax, top-k, and marginal-inclusion thresholding. The new applications reuse the applicable rules, excluding marginal-inclusion thresholding because these are not variable-selection tasks. Rashomon-set enumeration is discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: New protocols include clustering with 30 observations per dataset, 10,000 bags of size 25, and an elbow-based selector; decision-tree evaluation subsamples 50 of 547 cells and uses 10,000 bags of size 45. Tree comparisons ignore numerical split thresholds and retain exact ties. Settings for the retained experiments are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix H adds a structural case study of the three most frequent decision trees, contrasting disjoint feature choices with a one-split alternative in Figure 17. The existing regression and Lotka–Volterra bag-count sensitivity analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Existing trial counts and empirical-CDF reporting are retained. The added experiments follow the same independent-dataset or single-dataset leave-one-out reporting practices; they introduce no new confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial results for the new tasks. Clustering at ε = 0.3 has reported worst-case instability 0.067 and average set size 1.18. In Table 4, the inflated argmax and top-2 both have decision-tree instability 0.12, with average set sizes 1.74 and 2.02 respectively. Retained numerical tables and matched experimental graphics are unchanged.

T1.justification: The stability definition, inflated-argmax definition, Theorem 1, and existing derivations are retained. v3 explicitly points to the previously cited proof but adds no new proof or guarantee. Standard clustering and tree formulas explain the new experimental base algorithms.

C1.justification: Both versions claim generic model-selection stability through bagging and the inflated argmax, with adaptive, compact model sets. The additional clustering and decision-tree illustrations support the already-stated generality rather than establish a new central contribution or stronger guarantee.

C2.justification: Sections 2.3 and 6 add substantive qualifications: finite experiments cannot establish the universal stability property, and large returned sets can satisfy the overlap criterion while sharing only one model. v3 also discusses handling multiple models, performance versus stability, and how graph accuracy depends on regularization and domain knowledge.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-repository address and substantial setup information for the new applications, including Gaussian-mixture parameters, elbow-selector pseudocode and tolerances, tree software defaults, and model-matching conventions. Algorithm 2 nevertheless leaves its initial SSD value and signed-slope stopping convention unclear.

R1.justification: Related work expands to cover general model-selection literature, clustering stability, and Rashomon sets, with additional citations supporting the new applications. The central positioning as an adaptation of Soloff et al.'s inflated argmax remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 clarifies model-weight interpretation, utility-weighted accuracy, and the existing use of STRidge; it also updates affiliations and reorganizes the discussion. Graph cross-validation moves from Appendix D.2 to Appendix F. Most retained prose and the main section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v3 adds the clustering results and dataset figures, gene-correlation and decision-tree figures, Table 4, and Algorithm 2. Existing figures are resized or relocated, several captions move beside their figures, and tables are reformatted. Retained experimental graphics preserve their content.

improvement.justification: v3 better supports the framework's claimed generality with non-variable-selection applications and more clearly explains the limitations of overlap-based stability. The code pointer and implementation details also help readers assess reproducibility. These gains are tempered by the new elbow pseudocode: Algorithm 2 uses an undefined SSD0 and an unclear signed-slope cutoff with positive tolerance, leaving the clustering procedure incompletely specified.
